about: The work that remains, one item per gap, in the order it is planned (decision 0016). Rendered into Docs/TODO.md and the progress page by scripts/gen-progress.py; edit this file, never the outputs. `priority`: next (Phase 8, in order) | soon (the gap sweep after it: what ordinary apps hit) | later (needs a decision, a new subsystem or a platform that does not exist yet; Phase 9 works them in the file's order, decision 0018). `status`: planned | in-progress | done (with the date) | wontfix (a documented non-goal, with the reason in `detail`). `kind`: missing (no API) | accepted (API compiles, no behaviour) | approximate (behaves, pixels or motion differ) | verify (behaves, never measured against Apple) | infra (tooling, docs, site). Move an item to done when its support row changes; keep it here so the page shows what landed.

items.title: layoutOptions and safe areas through the seam
items.detail: `_PlatformViewRepresentableLayoutOptions` (`propagatesSafeArea`, the default): a representable's UIKit tree gets the part of its frame under a SwiftUI bar or inset as its window's safe area, and `UIHostingController.safeAreaRegions` hands the controller's safe area (a navigation or tab bar's) to the hosted runtime. Measured on the simulator under a navigation bar (ios/representable/safearea*, hostingsafearea*), with the safe area's geometric rule for every view (Position.md).

items.title: Environment to trait collection
items.detail: colorScheme is userInterfaceStyle, dynamicTypeSize the content size category, layoutDirection and the size classes follow through `UITraitOverrides`; `updateUIView` runs when they change (ios/representable/traits, ios/dark/representable-controls).

items.title: Hover inside a representable
items.detail: SwiftUI's pointer moves reach the hosted tree as a hover (`UIHoverGestureRecognizer` events) and the hovered view's `UIPointerInteraction` style or a button's pointer effect becomes the host cursor (ios/representable/hover, Playwright/representable-hover-probe.mjs, RepresentableTests).

items.title: Wheel scrolling of a hosted UIScrollView
items.detail: ios/representable/wheel (a UIScrollView in a representable inside a SwiftUI ScrollView) and Playwright/wheel-probe.mjs: a wheel over the inner scroll view moves it by the delta while the outer holds; past its end the outer takes the rest.

items.title: Animations across the seam
items.detail: `context.transaction` carries the SwiftUI animation into `updateUIView`; a `withAnimation` that resizes a representable lays the UIKit view out at every tweened size; `UIView.animate` inside `updateUIView` runs on the outer clock, advanced once per host frame for every representable. `RepresentableTests` on the headless clock.

items.title: Representables in lists, forms, scroll views and sheets
items.detail: ios/representable/list, form and scroll on the simulator: row heights and the hosted views' frames exact (a header-less grouped section sits 35 below the previous card, which the runtime now does). A representable in a sheet joins sw-ios-sheets.

items.title: Dismantle and coordinator lifecycle tests
items.detail: `RepresentableTests` and ios/representable/lifecycle: make, update, dismantle order at first sight, on an identity change (the new coordinator, view and update come before the old view's dismantle) and on removal; every evaluation of the parent's body updates the view; the coordinator is made once per node, outlives updates and dies with the node.

items.title: UIHostingConfiguration: margins, self-sizing, configuration state
items.detail: Measured on the simulator (ios/representable/hostingmargins, hostingcollection, hostingstate): default margins 15 above and below, a table row's fit plus its separator point, self-sizing collection list cells exactly the fit, and the cell's configuration state (`configurationUpdateHandler`, `updateConfiguration(using:)`, `setNeedsUpdateConfiguration`, now in UIKitWeb for table and collection cells) rebuilding the hosted content on selection.

items.title: UIHostingController in containers
items.detail: ios/representable/hostingnav, hostingsizing and UIHostingControllerTests: a hosting controller under a navigation or tab bar sees the bars' safe area (ix-layout-options); navigationTitle and toolbar items drive its navigationItem as titled bar buttons whose taps run the actions; sizingOptions keep the preferred size and invalidate the intrinsic size; rootView set under withAnimation tweens. A representable is re-measured only when its value, environment or proposal changes.

items.title: Image(uiImage:) for rendered images
items.detail: ios/representable/renderedimage: a UIImage from UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawn by Image (at its size, resizable, as a template in the foreground colour; withTintColor alone keeps the colours, as measured), and pngData() rasterised by the host (a canvas in the browser, CoreGraphics natively).

items.title: Trim the wasm bundle: Foundation
items.detail: Asked for 300 KB of headroom under the 3 MB budget by trimming the symbol and font tables; the tables measured 60 KB brotli and the cost was FoundationEssentials, whose members link whole (6.3 MB raw for a `Calendar`). Decision 0017: the `WebFoundation` module's stand-ins for `Data`, `URL`, `Calendar`, `TimeZone`, `Locale`, `DateComponents`, `IndexPath` and the sort comparators shadow FoundationEssentials' on wasm; Counter 3.05 MB to about 2.1 MB brotli, UIKitCounter 2.24 MB to 1.46 MB.

items.detail: Interface Builder archives are undocumented binary formats; apps port their scenes to code. Non-goal.

items.title: IME, autofill and VoiceOver by hand
items.detail: Japanese and Chinese IMEs and Safari autofill through the overlay input (spike 0.12's risk), a VoiceOver session in Safari; the findings recorded per browser in the matrix.

items.title: WebFoundation's gaps against Foundation
items.detail: The wasm stand-ins (decision 0017) cover what the frameworks and ordinary apps call. Done 2026-10-09 (Phase 9, item 1): `String(data:encoding:)` and `data(using:)` over WebFoundation's Data (UTF-8/16/32, ASCII, Latin 1, Windows-1252), `URLComponents` and `URLQueryItem`, Punycoded international host names, named time zones with daylight saving answered by the browser's Intl, Locale.current from the browser, the arithmetical calendars (Buddhist, Japanese, Minguo, Islamic civil and tabular, Persian, Hebrew, Coptic, Ethiopic, Indian, ISO 8601), `wrappingComponents`, `Date.FormatStyle` with its styles and symbols, ISO 8601, relative and verbatim styles, parse strategies, `DateFormatter` and `RelativeDateTimeFormatter`, `Data` slices that keep their indices; every core held to Foundation on macOS. Still different: English symbols in every locale, the Chinese calendar (Gregorian fields) and Umm al-Qura (tabular), UTS #46 mapping beyond case, lossy ASCII transliteration, `text.data(using:)` needing a typed result.

items.title: Right-to-left layout direction
items.detail: `layoutDirection` through stacks, grids, custom layouts, `layoutDirectionBehavior` on shapes, alignment guides and the text layouter; goldens from a right-to-left environment. Done 2026-10-09 (Phase 9, item 2): every container mirrors its placements once per level (ViewNode.place; the root and presenters excepted), so stacks, Spacer, leading padding and alignment, ZStack, Grid, LazyVGrid, a custom Layout, alignment guides, offset and position all mirror and a left-to-right island stays as written (layout/rtl-stacks, rtl-grid, rtl-custom exact); text alignment follows the direction (rtl-text); `Shape.layoutDirectionBehavior` (.mirrors by default, .fixed) and `flipsForRightToLeftLayoutDirection` (images do not flip by default; rtl-shapes); a horizontal ScrollView starts at its trailing end with natural swipes (rtl-scroll); progress bars, sliders and switches mirror their parts (RTLTests). Not mirrored, as measured: UnitPoints and gradients. Open: the ellipsis of a truncated right-aligned line, bidirectional text itself (the layouter has no bidi), the iOS navigation chrome in RTL.

items.title: Dynamic Type
items.detail: `dynamicTypeSize` and the content size categories: the text-style tables at every category (measured on the simulator), `ScaledMetric`, the environment from the host's setting. Done 2026-10-11 (Phase 9, item 3): the iOS profile's text styles take the category's point size and line (`iOSDynamicTypeSizes`, `iOSScaledTextStyleMetrics`; `ios/text/dynamic-xsmall`, `-xxxlarge`, `-ax4` exact in Tier A, B and C), multi-line heights at a category round up from the unrounded line, `@ScaledMetric` scales by the style's line-height ratio to the display scale, `dynamicTypeSize(_ range:)` clamps (`-clamped`), macOS ignores Dynamic Type (`text/dynamic-type`), iOS Safari's `-apple-system-body` sets the root size and UIKit's category. Open: controls, bars and list rows at other categories, `Font.custom(relativeTo:)`, the multi-line rounding rule for unscaled fonts.

items.title: Subviews-based ForEach and Group
items.detail: `ForEach(subviews:)`, `ForEach(sections:)`, `Group(subviews:)`, `containerValues`; the iOS 18 container APIs. Done 2026-10-11 (Phase 9, item 4): the children are resolved from the view value (tuples, ForEach with ids, conditionals, optionals, groups, AnyView, sections, modifiers on a container applied to each child, custom views through a multi-child body), `ContainerValues` with `@Entry`, `containerValue(_:_:)` and `tag(_:)`, `SubviewsCollection` slices as views; four macOS goldens exact (`foreach/subviews`, `-foreach`, `foreach/sections`, `foreach/container-values`), `SubviewsTests`. Open: lazy containers resolve eagerly; `List` and `Picker` do not read container values.

items.title: Layout protocol corners
items.detail: `Layout.Animatable` (animating layout parameters), `updateCache` reuse across passes and invalidation on environment changes, `GridLayout` as a `Layout` value, rows with more cells than the widest earlier row combined with spans. Done 2026-10-11 (Phase 9, item 5): a layout's animatable data tweens with a layout pass per frame, one cache per node updated on changes (remade for a new AnyLayout type), `GridLayout` over the shared `_GridPlanner` (`customlayout/grid-layout` identical to `Grid`), the growing-rows-with-spans case measured and matching (`grid/growing-spans`); `LayoutAnimationTests`. items.title: Safe area corners
items.detail: `GeometryProxy.safeAreaInsets`, `safeAreaInset` applied per list element, scroll indicators stopping at the inset; the keyboard region is a documented non-region in a browser. `ignoresSafeArea` on a view whose safe-area modifier hugs it on every edge extends on every edge by the geometric rule (PositionTests): a consequence, not a measurement. Done 2026-10-11 (Phase 9, item 6): a `GeometryReader` extends into the safe area it sits under and `proxy.safeAreaInsets` reports it (zero when ignoring), `safeAreaInset` on a list makes one inset view per element painted over it, indicator tracks stop at the inset, the keyboard region is documented as none in a browser (`position/safe-area-geometry`, `position/safe-area-elements`, `SafeAreaTests`).

items.title: Shape corners: strokedPath, container shapes, roles
items.detail: `Path.strokedPath` as the offset outline (polygons per segment today), `ContainerRelativeShape` following its container, `Shape.role` (stub), `Path(cgPath:)` on Apple platforms. Done 2026-10-11 (Phase 9, item 7): `strokedPath` is the CoreGraphics offset outline element for element on lines (curves flattened), `Path.boundingRect` tight, `ContainerRelativeShape` resolves through `containerShape` by the smallest edge inset drawn in the view's rect, the separator role draws hierarchical levels at the primary level, `Path(_ cgPath:)`/`cgPath` on Apple platforms (`shape/corners`, `ShapeTests`).

items.title: Elliptical and mesh gradients
items.detail: `EllipticalGradient`, `MeshGradient`, `ShapeStyle.in(_:)`, gradient `opacity`, repeat and mirror options (accepted), gradients on images and symbols, the hierarchical fade levels (approximate). Done 2026-10-11 (Phase 9, item 8): EllipticalGradient (display kind elliptical), MeshGradient rasterised into a bitmap (display op drawBitmap with a pixel side table to the Canvas2D painter), ShapeStyle.in / opacity / levels on gradients and AnyShapeStyle, gradients on symbols and template images; measured on NSHostingView renders (`gradient/corners`, `GradientTests`). Open: mesh animation and Bézier control points.

items.title: Animated effects and drawing groups
items.detail: Effect values under animation, `drawingGroup(opaque:colorMode:)` (accepted), filtering of content painted outside its frame, `drawingGroup`'s rasterisation semantics. Done 2026-10-11 (Phase 9, item 9): colour-effect amounts, blur radii and shadows tween under withAnimation, filter and blend boxes cover what a view paints outside its frame (the painted extent, strokes by their outline), drawingGroup's opaque and colorMode measured as no visible change (`effects/corners`, `EffectsTests`).

items.title: First frame and large lists
items.detail: The gallery and progress bundles' first frame on a slow connection, laziness in lists and lazy stacks (sw-lazy, sw-list-looks), a frame budget probe in CI over Examples/Landing. Done 2026-10-12 (Phase 9, item 44): List rows lazy like the lazy stacks', the bundles and first frames measured (Docs/elements/Performance.md: 4 MB gzip, about 21 s on 1.6 Mbps; the first frame 550-850 ms after the resources; scroll frames 7 ms median), scripts/frame-budget.sh and Playwright/frame-budget.mjs gating the landing page in CI (first frame 3 s, scroll median 40 ms); open: releasing far-away lazy elements, a smaller substrate. Found by Ember (2026-10-22): one layout of a sixty-comment thread (LazyVStack of rows that are an HStack of a VStack of HStacks of buttons with labels, each comment's HTML as AttributedString Texts) takes ~2.5 s in release and ~10 s in debug — 800 000 sizeThatFits calls, because nested stacks measure each child at the cross product of the widths and heights their parents probe (a Text sees 40 distinct proposals, 7 widths × 8 heights; Text's height proposal matters for its line trimming, so its memo cannot drop it). The thread settles after one layout; scrolling it relayouts. Open: fewer probes per level (a stack's min/max probes along its axis need not vary with every cross proposal), or a per-node memo keyed on what the node's measurement depends on. 2026-10-25 (Docs/elements/Performance.md, "A real app's frames"): the thread's cost was the lazy stack distributing its height (fixed: a lazy stack proposes nothing along its axis) and a stack proposing shares no memo matches (fixed: a one-size or bounded child takes its infinite answer); every scrolled frame had been a memo-dropping layout from a spinner's tick (repaint now), every update dropped every memo (an updated node's ancestry now), and blurs and shadows painted the whole canvas (their boxes now). Ember: feed scroll 80 → 18 ms a frame, thread 125 → 13–18, a lazy row 190–390 → 45, a full thread layout 1.5 s → 112 ms. Still open: ~10 µs a measurement (a release profile with names), updates that re-evaluate a whole screen. 2026-10-28: on the phone Ember was still seconds a frame — WebKit's canvas has no `filter`, so every blur ran the painter's per-pixel JavaScript Gaussian (σ 60 under a material bar at DPR 3: two thousand million multiplies a bar, two bars a frame; 430 ms a frame in Playwright's WebKit); the fallback draws the box down by ⌊σ/4⌋ and blurs by box passes (WebKit paint 420 → 7–11 ms, as Chrome).

items.title: `import Foundation` on wasm
items.detail: Done 2026-10-12 (Phase 10, item 1, decision 0021): `Packages/Shadows` holds a module named `Foundation` that re-exports WebFoundation, WASILibc, Observation and Combine; an app's Package.swift links it `.when(platforms: [.wasi])` (README, Examples/Launches) — it cannot be a dependency of the `SwiftUI` target, because SwiftPM's wasm test discovery imports XCTest, whose binary module wants the SDK's Foundation (`_BridgedStoredNSError`, `NSObject`, `FileHandle` in the generated runner). The SwiftUI shim re-exports WebFoundation and WASILibc itself, so `import SwiftUI` alone gives libm as Apple's does; WebFoundation declares `DispatchQueue` (main and global work on the main actor through the host's executor, `asyncAfter`, `sync` in place, groups, work items, `DispatchTime`) and its own `LocalizedError` (naming FoundationEssentials' protocol descriptor extracted CocoaError.swift and 3.3 MB of FoundationEssentials into the Gallery); WebFoundation gains `UserDefaults` (suites as JSON in localStorage through the host), `Bundle` (`main`, SwiftPM's `Bundle.module` accessor compiles, resource URLs under the bundle's assets, where build-wasm.sh now copies a target's processed resources), `FileManager` with durable `file:` URLs (base64 in localStorage), `JSONEncoder`/`JSONDecoder` over the project's coder (moved to WebFoundation as JSONCoder.swift), `NSError` and `Error.localizedDescription`; `Color(_:bundle:)` and `Image(_:bundle:)` take the label everywhere. The 2048 port keeps its `import Foundation` files and its libm calls, Scrumdinger builds with its real FileService, `Bundle.module` and `@Observable` unpatched; `Examples/Launches` (a model importing Foundation and Combine: UserDefaults, FileManager + JSONEncoder, a Combine chain, a dispatched delay, libm, Bundle) runs in CI's browser job through `Playwright/launches-probe.mjs` across three loads. Counter 2,934,562 → 2,967,145 brotli with pf-combine-module. The Node test runner cannot await the event loop, so the queued dispatch forms are covered by the Launches probe. Open: strategies on the JSON coders, `UserDefaults.didChangeNotification`, file attributes and dates, macOS native's `import Foundation` + `import SwiftUI` ambiguity (pf-combine-module). Originally: An app file that imports Foundation next to SwiftUI fails on wasm: URL, Data, DateFormatter and NumberFormatter are ambiguous between the SDK's Foundation and WebFoundation's stand-ins (decision 0017), and libm (`log2`, `pow`), Dispatch, Observation (`@Observable` under `import Foundation`) and `Bundle` are out of scope where Apple's Foundation re-exports them. A package module named `Foundation`, linked only on wasm, that re-exports WebFoundation, WASILibc, Observation and Dispatch and declares `Bundle` (`main`, `module` for SPM resource targets, `url(forResource:)`), with the `bundle:` labels on `Color` and `Image`; SPM's generated resource accessor then compiles too. All three surveyed apps hit this.

items.title: `import Combine` on wasm
items.detail: Done 2026-10-12 (Phase 10, item 2, decision 0021): the ObservableObject family and the publishers moved out of SwiftUIWebCore into `WebCombine` (Packages/WebGraphics, built everywhere; SwiftUIWebCore and the SwiftUI shim re-export it), the `Publisher` protocol gained completion and failure, the subjects send from any isolation (Combine's `send` is nonisolated) and a `Combine` module in Packages/Shadows re-exports it on wasm, linked by an app's Package.swift (and the shadow Foundation re-exports Combine, as Apple's does); `sink` and `assign` are nonisolated with plain closures as Combine's, so a nonisolated model subscribes in its initialiser: `AnyPublisher`, `Cancellable`, `Future`, `Deferred`, `Empty`, `Fail`, `Sequence.publisher`, `sink(receiveCompletion:)`, `assign`, and the operators (map, tryMap, compactMap, scan, filter, removeDuplicates, first, last, dropFirst, prefix, collect, mapError, setFailureType, catch, replaceError, retry, merge, combineLatest, zip, prepend, append, debounce, delay, throttle, timeout, share, handleEvents, print, values) as `_Pipe`s over the closure subscriptions; schedulers accepted and ignored. SwiftUI-2048 compiles with its `import Combine` and its nonisolated model; the Countries app moves on to UserNotifications; `Examples/Launches` subscribes from a nonisolated model and its probe reads the chained status. WebCombineTests natively; the shadow itself through the Launches probe (SwiftPM's wasm test discovery rules the shadows out of this package's tests). Also: a `@StateObject` (or `@State`) declared on the `App` struct is one instance for the process and a change re-reads the app's body, updating the main window's root in place (`_appRemount`; before, every access to the property made a new object and the body was read once). Open: `Subscriber`/`Subscription`, `Scheduler`, `assign(to: &$published)`, Apple's operator type names, the macOS native ambiguity of `import Foundation` + `import SwiftUI` (Apple's Combine stays there). Originally: `import Combine` is `no such module` on wasm; the Combine-free publishers live in SwiftUIWebCore (Just, the subjects, Timer.publish, objectWillChange, `$published`) without operators, `AnyPublisher`, `Cancellable` or a completion path, and `PassthroughSubject.send` is @MainActor where Combine's is nonisolated. A `Combine` module, linked only on wasm, over the same publishers: `AnyPublisher`/`eraseToAnyPublisher`, `Cancellable`, `map`, `filter`, `compactMap`, `removeDuplicates`, `first`, `Publishers.Merge`, `CombineLatest`, `Fail`, `Future`, `sink(receiveCompletion:receiveValue:)`, `store(in: &Set<AnyCancellable>)`, `assign`, `debounce` and `receive(on:)`; completion and failure through the subscription. 2048 and Countries import it; on macOS native Apple's Combine stays and `import Foundation` + `import SwiftUI` leaves ObservableObject ambiguous (recorded, not solved here).

Scrumdinger's add/edit sheets lose their Dismiss and Add buttons. Also an image-only toolbar Button gets an empty accessibility label (SwiftUI derives it from the symbol name). Goldens: a sheet with an inline untitled bar and items, from the simulator. Done 2026-10-12: the stack in a sheet has its own bar 5.5 lower (ios/sheet/nav, ios/sheet/nav-titled from iOS 27; the whole ios/sheet/ family regenerated there, the card now starts at 21), an empty title is an inline bar with nothing drawn, a title inside a presentation stays off the window's, and on iOS toolbar items go to the nearest stack's bar as 36 pt pills (the window bar is macOS only); sheet content clipped to the card. IOSSheetNavigationTests tap the pills. The image-only button's accessibility label is still open (sw-toolbar-symbol-label).

items.detail: `@UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor` (and the `UISceneConfiguration.delegateClass` / `UIWindowSceneDelegate` route to a scene delegate), `UIApplication.keyboardWillShowNotification` / `keyboardWillHideNotification` with `UIResponder.keyboardFrameEndUserInfoKey` (the host's text input focus), `UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`, `UIBackgroundFetchResult`, `UIMenuBuilder` and `UIMenu.Identifier` as accepted. A non-final `UIApplicationDelegate` still needs `required init()` and `#selector` has no equivalent (documented). Done 2026-10-12 against the Countries app's sources: `@UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor` (SwiftUIWebUIKit) makes one delegate with the App value and runs UIKit's launch through `UIKitScene.launchApplication` — willFinish/didFinish, the notification, `configurationForConnecting` whose `UISceneConfiguration.delegateClass` becomes the scene delegate, connection and activation; an ObservableObject delegate goes into every window's environment (`_appEnvironmentObjects`); the page's visibility and focus reach the scene delegate (`Runtime._hostLifecycleObservers`). `UIWindowSceneDelegate.window` optional as UIKit's; `UIBackgroundFetchResult`, the remote-notification delegate methods with `registerForRemoteNotifications` failing through the delegate (no push service in a page), `openSettingsURLString` (opens nothing, answers false), the keyboard notifications with UIKit's user-info keys driven by `UIKitScene.keyboardFrame` (`NSValue`/`NSNumber` on wasm). The browser host (2026-10-13, KeyboardHost.swift in SwiftUIWebCanvas): `UIKitScene.keyboardFrame` from `window.visualViewport` against `window.innerHeight` through `_KeyboardFrameEstimator` (UIKitWebCore) — only while a text input or textarea has the focus, at scale 1 (a pinch zoom is not the keyboard), with at least 80 pt below the visual viewport (the URL bar's collapse is not), and an ordinary resize moves both viewports together so reports nothing; re-read on the visual viewport's resize/scroll, focusin/focusout and the window's resize; the screen is the page (the window's size). Evidence, kept apart: (1) KeyboardFrameTests (UIKitWeb, 7) on synthetic readings — up, scrolled-while-editing, down, unfocused, zoomed, resized, the URL bar, a tall page — and the notifications out; (2) the Launches probe in desktop Chromium on SYNTHETIC readings through `__swiftuiwebDebug.syntheticKeyboardReading` (a plain `setViewportSize` leaves the app's line at 0; a focused reading 336 short shows `keyboard: 336` read as the Countries handler reads `keyboardFrameEndUserInfoKey`, at the band 164,336; zoom and an unfocused reading show none) — the host→scene→notification path, not a keyboard; (3) the phone's own keyboard: `Playwright/device-keyboard.mjs` through safaridriver — NOT OBTAINED: the paired iPhone could not be used by safaridriver in this session ('Some devices were found, but could not be used', the phone is `available`, not `connected` — it needs the user), and the iOS 27 Simulator session was inconclusive (WebDriver's element click and a touch sequence both left the field unfocused while a scripted focus() took focus without raising a keyboard; the run says `inconclusive`). The real-keyboard claim stays open until that script passes on the phone. The modes this reads: iOS Safari and Chrome on Android since 108, whose default `interactive-widget=resizes-visual` shrinks the visual viewport alone (developer.chrome.com/blog/viewport-resize-behavior). Not seen by the host, and said so rather than guessed: `resizes-content` (Chrome before 108 and Android WebView by default) shrinks the layout viewport with the visual one — the page gets shorter, the viewports agree, nothing is reported; `overlays-content` shrinks neither — a viewport difference cannot see an overlay, nothing is reported; `UIScreen.main.bounds` is not kept to the window for a SwiftUI app (390×844 default; the host sizes the band from the window instead). Tests: SceneLifecycleTests, KeyboardFrameTests (UIKitWeb), UIApplicationDelegateAdaptorTests.

items.title: URLSession over fetch
items.detail: URLSession over the host's fetch (2026-10-13, decision 0021), written against the Countries app's WebRepository: URLSession(configuration:) and .shared, URLSessionConfiguration (timeouts, additional headers, cache policy and urlCache recorded; the browser's cache serves fetch), URLRequest (method, headers case-insensitively, body, timeout, cache policy), data(for:)/data(from:)/upload/download(from:) (a temporary file under /tmp) and the dataTask forms with resume/cancel/state, URLResponse/HTTPURLResponse (status, headers, mime type, localizedString(forStatusCode:)), URLError with Foundation's codes. The semantics an app relies on, kept apart: an HTTP error status is a response with its status, headers and bytes — never an error; a transport failure, a CORS refusal (the browser hides the response), a timeout or a cancellation is a thrown URLError (-1004 cannotConnectToHost with the browser's message, -1001, -999, -1009 offline) — never a status. The core (_WebURLSession, platform-independent) is tested against a fake host (URLSessionCoreTests); the wasm types over it in WasmFoundationTests; the browser host (NetworkHost.swift: fetch, AbortController, the timeout, the final URL after the browser's redirects) in Examples/Launches against local fixtures in CI — a same-origin JSON (200, decoded, application/json), a missing path (404 as a response with a body), a second local server without CORS headers (-1004, no status), a cancelled task (-999). Not done: streaming bodies, delegates (authentication, redirects — the browser follows them itself), background sessions, cookies beyond the browser's own, WebSocket tasks, URLCache contents. External dependency, verified 2026-10-12 and kept apart from this implementation: the Countries app's pinned GET https://restcountries.com/v2/all?fields=name,translations,population,flag,alpha3Code answers 301 → https://files-03.restcountries.com/countries.00/legacy.json → 200 with a 261-byte body {"success": false, "errors": ["This API version has been deprecated … migrate to … v5"]} (curl, with and without a browser user agent), with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header anywhere in the chain; from an isolated Chrome 155 page at the app origin, fetch() fails with TypeError: Failed to fetch (net::ERR_FAILED), i.e. a CORS failure before any response is readable. A URLSession over fetch would therefore surface that failure to the app's CountriesWebRepository exactly as iOS would surface a network error; the app's own error view is the honest outcome. No endpoint rewrite, proxy or credentials; whether the service's state is permanent is not established.

items.title: SwiftData
items.detail: SwiftData written against the Countries app's models and repositories (2026-10-13, decision 0021): the `@Model`, `@Attribute`, `@Relationship`, `@Transient`, `#Predicate`, `@ModelActor` and `@Query` macros (SwiftDataMacros; `@Query` is a macro as Apple's — a property wrapper cannot infer the element type), `Schema` with its version, `ModelConfiguration`, `ModelContainer` with its `@MainActor` `mainContext`, `ModelContext` (insert as an upsert by `@Attribute(.unique)` — the stored instance keeps its identity and takes the values, a fresh related instance resolves to the stored one; delete unlinking inverses; fetch with the in-memory `#Predicate`, sort descriptors, limit and offset; `transaction` saving once at its end; autosave; `save`), inverse relationships kept from either side's `inverse:` declaration and through the setters, `PersistentIdentifier`, `FetchDescriptor`, `SortDescriptor`, `ModelActor` with its own context, cross-context sync (a model actor's save reaches the main context's next fetch and its `@Query` at the main actor's next turn), `modelContainer(_:)`/`modelContainer(for:)`/`modelContext(_:)`, `EnvironmentValues.modelContext`. Persistence: a container that is not in-memory-only writes one JSON document per store through the host (localStorage under `swiftuiweb.swiftdata.<name>` in the browser, DataHost.swift) at every save and reads it at open, identifiers kept; an in-memory container is its own (two of one name share nothing). Honest failures: a persistent configuration with no host storage or storage the page is denied (DataHost catches the browser's SecurityError on `localStorage` itself and on `getItem`, QuotaExceededError on `setItem`, in JavaScript — a Swift error, never a trap), bytes that are not a store, or a store written by another schema version do not open (`SwiftDataError.storageUnavailable`/`corruptStore`/`incompatibleSchema`; the stored bytes stay untouched — no migration); a host write the browser refuses fails the save and leaves the changes pending. Proof: SwiftDataTests (13, the app's models verbatim in shape and its repository's flows: upsert, both-sided inverses, delete, predicate/sort, reopen with relationships, independence, autosave counts, `@Query` after an actor's save, the Query+Search helper) and Examples/Launches in Chromium (a Visit with its Note per launch, three reloads counted from localStorage, a second container of the name reading the save). The Countries app's own container opens in the browser (the hosts now install before the App value is made); its list stays blocked on its deprecated service (pf-urlsession), so none of this is a Countries pass. Not SwiftData: no SQL (predicates run as closures over the models in memory), no faulting, no migration plans, no CloudKit, no undo, no `enumerate`/batch APIs; `modelContainer(for:)` reports a failed open to `onSetup` and the view then has a non-persistent context (Apple's traps). The Countries app was retired 2026-10-22 (decision 0021); its probe is gone with it, the SwiftData proofs (SwiftDataTests, the Launches example) stay.

items.title: Durable files on wasm
items.detail: Partly done 2026-10-12 with pf-foundation-module: `FileManager`'s directories, `Data.write(to:)`/`Data(contentsOf:)` on file URLs and `UserDefaults` persist through the browser host in localStorage (a few MB in all). Open: `@AppStorage` and `@SceneStorage` do not exist yet (over UserDefaults, with the scene's id), the origin private file system for large files and binary data without base64, `FileManager` attributes, dates and enumerators, `UserDefaults.didChangeNotification` and key-value observing. Originally: `FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory)`, `Data.write(to:)` and `Data(contentsOf:)`, `UserDefaults` and `@AppStorage` compile on wasm but nothing survives a reload (Scrumdinger's FileService loads 'The file doesn't exist' and could not save). A document directory backed by the origin private file system (or localStorage for small files), and UserDefaults over localStorage.

items.title: Speech, audio and notifications for the web
items.detail: Superseded 2026-10-12 (the apps run unmodified or not at all; nothing on the app's side is swapped): the frameworks Scrumdinger and the Countries app reach for get real web behaviour in modules of the same name — `pf-avfoundation-audio`, `pf-speech`, `pf-usernotifications`. What stayed out of reach for a while was the compiler, not the web: `@objc` and `#selector` are rejected by the stock wasm SDK ("Objective-C interoperability is disabled"; forcing `-enable-objc-interop` crashes the frontend). DONE 2026-10-23: the three modules are real (`pf-avfoundation-audio`, `pf-usernotifications` 2026-10-12, `pf-speech` 2026-10-23 with decision 0022's on-device recogniser), and the compiler barrier fell to the Objective-C runtime wasm SDK (decision 0023) — see `ap-app-ports`, all three apps pass.

items.title: Open-source apps as a check
items.detail: The four upstream trees (the three apps and the Countries app's EnvironmentOverrides dependency) are git submodules at pinned commits under `Apps/upstream/`, with a SHA-256 manifest per tree; `Apps/Package.swift` mirrors each upstream target (sources, language mode, excludes and resources) and links this package's products, nothing else (`Apps/README.md`). `scripts/check-apps.sh` verifies the pins and that no upstream file differs, then builds each app for wasm; CI runs it. Done: the baseline and the script. CI (the browser job) checks the submodules out and runs `--verify`, builds Scrumdinger for wasm and runs `Playwright/scrumdinger-probe.mjs`, three separate steps. Scrumdinger compiles from its unmodified sources (2026-10-12) and its add sheet, attendee, persistence across a reload and detail screen run in Chromium; its meeting is blocked on speech (pf-speech). Open: the Countries app (EnvironmentOverrides' UIKit gaps first), and SwiftUI-2048's `AppDelegate.swift`, which the wasm compiler refuses (`@objc`, `#selector`): the source-preserving routes are design-level — an Objective-C runtime for wasm with an interop-enabled toolchain, or an upstream compiler relaxation accepting `@objc`/`#selector` without a runtime (decision 0021); excluding or rewriting the file, replacing the entry point, a native-only acceptance or another app are not authorised. Countries (2026-10-12): EnvironmentOverrides now compiles (the smallest changes: @preconcurrency on UIScreen, the feedback generators and the image renderer as every UIKit class is from Objective-C — a Swift 5 mode app calls them from nonisolated helpers; UIView.drawHierarchy; UIImageWriteToSavedPhotosAlbum with a string-backed Selector; Bundle.localizations). The app's own gaps, from its build: @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor, UISceneConfiguration.delegateClass, UIWindowSceneDelegate, UIBackgroundFetchResult, UIApplication.keyboardWillShow/HideNotification, UIResponder.keyboardFrameEndUserInfoKey, UIApplication.openSettingsURLString (uk-app-delegate-adaptor); NSObject and NSValue on wasm (a delegate base class: pf-web-foundation-gaps); UserNotifications (pf-usernotifications); URLSession and URLSessionConfiguration (pf-urlsession); SwiftData's ModelContainer, Schema, FetchDescriptor, @ModelActor, modelContext, View.modelContainer (pf-swiftdata). No broad language-mode migration is needed for any of these. 2026-10-12 later: the delegate adaptor, keyboard notifications, NSObject/NSValue/NSNumber on wasm, percent encoding with the URL character sets and Combine's TopLevelDecoder landed; the Countries build's remaining 89 errors are all SwiftData (pf-swiftdata), URLSession/URLRequest/HTTPURLResponse (pf-urlsession) and UserNotifications (pf-usernotifications). After pf-usernotifications, NSLocalizedString and NSUserCancelledError (2026-10-12): 67 errors, all SwiftData (@Model, ModelContainer, FetchDescriptor, modelContext, the Hashable/Identifiable the macro gives) and URLSession/URLRequest/HTTPURLResponse/URLSessionConfiguration — plus the restcountries v2 endpoint's own state, recorded under pf-urlsession. After pf-urlsession (2026-10-13): the Countries build's remaining errors are SwiftData alone (52 unique: @Model, ModelContainer, FetchDescriptor, modelContext, #Predicate, @Query, the Hashable/Identifiable the macro gives) — pf-swiftdata. Even then the app's data comes from restcountries v2, which answers a deprecation notice without CORS headers: a URLError in the app's error view, not a country list. 2026-10-22: Countries retired (its restcountries v2 service is gone; the record stays in decision 0021 and Apps/README.md) and Ember (DatanoiseTV/ember-hackernews, MIT, pinned 1ed87d7f) took its place: it compiles from its unmodified sources and its ten flows pass in Chromium against the live Hacker News API (Playwright/ember-probe.mjs, full_app_pass true) — onboarding, the Top feed and chips, a discussion, save and Saved, search, Settings, a reload. What it asked for: WebKit's UIKit face, SafariServices and Security (Packages/Shadows), HTTPCookie, NSString bridging, NSRegularExpression over the browser's RegExp, JSONSerialization, the decoder's key and date strategies, Material, and the runtime fixes listed in the decision. Standing: SwiftUI-2048 passes with the Objective-C runtime SDK (decision 0023), Ember passes, Scrumdinger's meeting runs since 2026-10-23 (pf-speech, decision 0022: the on-device recogniser hears the app's appended buffers; the probe's microphone is Chrome's fake device playing a committed recording) — all three apps pass, full_app_pass true for each. 2026-10-29 (Corey on his iPhone: Dark could not be set, the sign-in sheet printed a URL): a SwiftUI app's launch registers a key UIWindow whose overrideUserInterfaceStyle drives the runtime's colour scheme (presentations follow at once); WKWebView in a representable is a host element at last (the iframe never existed), every framed page carries an Open ↗ link (sites that refuse framing paint nothing); a hosted controller's dismiss closes the SwiftUI sheet (SFSafariViewController's Done); a menu's items keep their titles in a toolbar; nine symbols mapped; UIApplication.open from SwiftUI; a Label's icon hidden from accessibility. The probe drives fourteen flows (dark mode, the reader and sign-in sheets, the More menu added). Out of reach on a static origin: the account features (HN refuses framing, its session cookie is cross-origin and HttpOnly, its posts have no CORS) — a same-origin proxy would be needed; favicons stay the globe fallback.

items.title: AVAudioPlayer, AVAudioSession, AVAudioEngine
items.detail: Scrumdinger's AudioService and SpeechService as written: `AVAudioPlayer(contentsOf:)`, `prepareToPlay`, `play`, `currentTime` over an HTMLAudioElement on the bundle's `ding.wav`; `AVAudioSession.sharedInstance()` with `setCategory(_:mode:options:)` and `setActive(_:options:)` accepted, `AVAudioApplication.requestRecordPermission` over `getUserMedia`; `AVAudioEngine` whose `inputNode` is the microphone (`outputFormat(forBus:)`, `installTap(onBus:bufferSize:format:)` delivering `AVAudioPCMBuffer`s from an AudioWorklet, `removeTap`, `prepare`, `start`, `stop`). The module exists (`AVPlayer` for AVKit); the native host plays through AVFoundation itself. Done 2026-10-12 (Sources/AVFoundation/AVAudio.swift, MediaHost.swift in SwiftUIWebCanvas; AVAudioAndSpeechTests against a fake host). Scrumdinger's AudioService and SpeechService compile and run against it; its meeting reaches neither the player nor the engine yet because the app asks for speech authorisation first (pf-speech).

items.title: Speech over the Web Speech API
items.detail: A `Speech` module written against Scrumdinger's SpeechService: `SFSpeechRecognizer(locale:)`, `requestAuthorization`, `isAvailable`, `recognitionTask(with:resultHandler:)` and the delegate form, `SFSpeechAudioBufferRecognitionRequest` (`shouldReportPartialResults`, `taskHint`, `addsPunctuation`, `append(_:)`, `endAudio()`), `SFSpeechRecognitionTask` (`cancel`, `finish`, `state`), `SFSpeechRecognitionResult`/`SFTranscription`/segments; a host supplies `_SpeechHost` (2026-10-12). What is NOT done, and not counted: a recogniser. The page's `SpeechRecognition` listens to a microphone stream of its own, not the PCM buffers the app appends from its audio tap, and in Chrome it sends the audio to Google's service — a different data flow and an external transmission nobody approved, so the browser host installs no recogniser at all and `isAvailable` is false (Scrumdinger shows its own "Not authorized to recognize speech" alert, which the Playwright flow expects). Faithful options, each consuming the app's appended buffers: (a) the buffers through an `AudioWorklet` into a `MediaStreamTrack` (`AudioContext.createMediaStreamDestination`) handed to `SpeechRecognition.start(track)` with `processLocally: true` (Chrome 138+/the on-device Web Speech additions; feature-detected, unavailable elsewhere) — the app's bytes, recognised on the device; (b) an in-page model (whisper.cpp or Vosk compiled to wasm) fed the buffers directly — the app's bytes, on the device, at the cost of a model download; (c) a server the deployer runs, given the buffers over the deployer's own connection — the app's bytes, but a transmission the deployer must approve. Which to build is a decision to put to Corey; none is implied by the stand-in's existence. Design draft with browser evidence, semantics and the buffer-dependence tests: Docs/decisions/0022-speech-from-appended-buffers.md (recommends option A: the appended buffers through an AudioWorklet track into Chromium's on-device recogniser; nothing built pending the decision). DONE 2026-10-23 (decision 0022, option A, chosen by Corey 2026-10-22): the host (SpeechHost.swift) recognises exactly the appended buffers — resampled to 16 kHz, played through an AudioWorklet into a MediaStreamTrack that Chrome's on-device SpeechRecognition (processLocally) listens to; requestAuthorization installs the locale's pack (the one download, from the browser's vendor); partial results are cumulative and the one final result comes when the audio ends. Proven by Playwright/speech-probe.mjs (Launches' SpeechCheck: two committed fixtures told apart, a 48 kHz copy resampled, silence and nothing empty, a cancel final-less, every result after its frames) and by Scrumdinger's meeting (full_app_pass true). Chromium-only by feature detection; isAvailable is false elsewhere. Two traps recorded in the decision: the recogniser transcribes a 16 kHz track and only hears a 48 kHz one, and Playwright's default --no-sandbox silences it (the probes launch the installed Chrome with chromiumSandbox: true).

items.title: UserNotifications over the Notification API
items.detail: `UNUserNotificationCenter.current()`, `requestAuthorization(options:)`, `notificationSettings()`/`getNotificationSettings`, `UNAuthorizationStatus`, delegate for a foreground presentation, over `Notification.requestPermission` and `new Notification`; `UIApplication.registerForRemoteNotifications` accepted with the delegate's failure callback (no push service). The Countries app's `UserPermissionsInteractor` and `PushNotificationsHandler`. Done 2026-10-12 against the Countries app's UserPermissionsInteractor and PushNotificationsHandler: UNUserNotificationCenter.current() with notificationSettings()/getNotificationSettings, requestAuthorization(options:) (closure and async), add(_:) of a local UNNotificationRequest delivered on the main actor after the trigger's interval, the delegate's willPresent deciding whether the host shows it and didReceive with the request's userInfo when the user opens it, pending and delivered lists, categories accepted; UNAuthorizationStatus/Options, UNNotificationSettings, content/trigger/request/response/presentation options. The browser host (NotificationsHost.swift) is the page's Notification API: Notification.permission, requestPermission() as the one prompt, new Notification for a delivered request, its click as the response; browsers without the API (iOS Safari outside a web app) leave no host — never authorised, nothing shown, as the tests say. No push service: UIApplication.registerForRemoteNotifications fails through the app delegate. UserNotificationsTests against a fake host.

items.title: Isolation annotations as Apple declares them
items.detail: A Swift 6 app compiles against this package as against Apple's only if every protocol, initializer and modifier carries the same isolation: the protocols Apple marks `@MainActor @preconcurrency` (ToolbarContent, the style protocols, Commands, Gesture, TabContent, the representables, AccessibilityRotorContent, DropDelegate) and not the ones it leaves nonisolated (ListStyle, PickerStyle, TextFieldStyle, DynamicViewContent, ScrollTargetBehavior); view initializers `nonisolated` (1 595 of Apple's are; 627 of ours were isolated), action parameters `@preconcurrency @MainActor` where Apple's are. Done 2026-10-12 for the protocols and for Button and Label (Scrumdinger's `ToolbarButton` and its `Button(_:symbol:)` wrappers would not compile); the sweep over the remaining initializers and modifiers against the SDK's swiftinterface is open. Found by the 2048 port (2026-10-13): `withTransaction` and `withAnimation` are `@MainActor` here and nonisolated in Apple's (upstream 2048's nonisolated `@objc func newGame` calls `withTransaction`).

items.title: Asset catalogs in the bundle
items.detail: Already there (decision 0011): `scripts/assets.py` reads every `*.xcassets` under the package into the bundle's manifest, colour sets with their appearances included, so Scrumdinger's sixteen theme colours resolve through `Color(_:bundle:)` (checked 2026-10-12: 16 colour sets from its three catalogs). `scripts/build-wasm.sh` gained `--product` for the Apps package and scopes the catalogs to the app's own upstream tree (three apps, three AccentColors).
